MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The sample space has 8 equally likely outcomes and at least two heads occurs in HHH, HHT, HTH and THH, so the probability is 4/8 = 1/2.

outcome.title: Calculate theoretical probability of single and compound events.

MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
A bag contains counters as listed:
| Colour | Count |
| Yellow | 6 |
| Black | 9 |
| White | 5 |

One counter is drawn at random. Find the probability that it is yellow or white.
MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: There are 20 counters and 11 are yellow or white, so the probability is 11/20.

outcome.title: Calculate theoretical probability of single and compound events.

MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Two fair dice are thrown together. Find the probability that the sum of the numbers appearing is 9.
MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: There are 36 equally likely outcomes and the sum 9 arises from (3,6), (4,5), (5,4) and (6,3), so the probability is 4/36 = 1/9.

outcome.title: Calculate theoretical probability of single and compound events.

MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: The probability of an impossible event is
MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: An impossible event has no favourable outcome, so its probability is 0.

MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
Assertion (A): The sum of the probabilities of all elementary events of an experiment is 1.
Reason (R): The elementary events together account for every outcome in the sample space exactly once.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Adding the probabilities of all elementary events counts the whole sample space once, which gives 1.

MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: State whether the following is true or false, and justify in one line: Classical probability assumes that all outcomes of the experiment are equally likely.
MATHEMATICS_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The classical definition divides favourable outcomes by total outcomes, which is valid only when the outcomes are equally likely.

outcome.title: Define life processes and explain why simple diffusion is inadequate for multicellular organisms.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Explain why simple diffusion alone cannot meet the oxygen requirement of a large multicellular animal, while it is sufficient for a single-celled organism such as an amoeba.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Because in a large body most cells are far from the surface, so diffusion is far too slow and the surface area to volume ratio is too small; a specialised transport system is needed.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Diffusion is effective only over very short distances. An amoeba has a high surface area to volume ratio and every part of its body is in contact with the surrounding water, so gases reach all of its cytoplasm quickly. In a large animal the inner cells are many centimetres from the surface and the surface area per unit volume is small, so oxygen would arrive far too slowly to sustain respiration, making circulatory and respiratory systems necessary.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Explain eye accommodation and correct Myopia, Hypermetropia, and Presbyopia using spherical lenses.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: A person suffering from myopia can see distinctly only up to 80 cm. Find the nature and power of the corrective lens required for distant vision.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: A concave lens of power -1.25 dioptre
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The lens must form the image of a distant object at the far point, so f = -80 cm = -0.8 m and P = 1/(-0.8) = -1.25 D, which is a diverging concave lens.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Explain eye accommodation and correct Myopia, Hypermetropia, and Presbyopia using spherical lenses.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: The ability of the eye lens to change its curvature and focus objects at different distances is called
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: accommodation
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Ciliary muscles alter the curvature and hence the focal length of the eye lens, and this ability is termed accommodation.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Explain eye accommodation and correct Myopia, Hypermetropia, and Presbyopia using spherical lenses.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: A person with hypermetropia has a near point of 50 cm. Find the power of the lens needed so that the person can read comfortably at the normal near point of 25 cm.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: +2 dioptre
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The lens must form a virtual image at 50 cm of an object placed at 25 cm, so 1/f = 1/(-50) - 1/(-25) = 1/50, f = +50 cm and P = 1/0.5 = +2 D, a converging convex lens.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Explain eye accommodation and correct Myopia, Hypermetropia, and Presbyopia using spherical lenses.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: State what presbyopia is and explain why a bifocal lens is commonly prescribed for it.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: It is the age-related loss of accommodation; a bifocal lens has a concave upper part for distant vision and a convex lower part for near vision.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: With age the ciliary muscles weaken and the eye lens becomes less flexible, so the near point recedes and distant vision may also be affected. A bifocal lens combines the two required corrections in one spectacle lens.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Explain eye accommodation and correct Myopia, Hypermetropia, and Presbyopia using spherical lenses.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Myopia is corrected by using
options: a bifocal lens in every case
a concave lens of suitable power
a convex lens of suitable power
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: a concave lens of suitable power
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: In myopia the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina, so a diverging concave lens is used to push the image back onto the retina.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Explain eye accommodation and correct Myopia, Hypermetropia, and Presbyopia using spherical lenses.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
A student reads a textbook easily but cannot read the writing on the classroom board from the last bench.

Name the defect of vision and the type of lens required, giving a reason.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Myopia, corrected with a concave lens.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The student's near vision is normal but distant vision is blurred, which is myopia. A concave lens diverges the incoming light so that the image of the distant board is formed on the retina rather than in front of it.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Explain eye accommodation and correct Myopia, Hypermetropia, and Presbyopia using spherical lenses.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
Assertion (A): The least distance of distinct vision for a normal adult eye is taken as 25 cm.
Reason (R): The eye lens can go on increasing its curvature without any limit.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: A is true but R is false.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The standard near point is indeed about 25 cm, but the curvature of the eye lens cannot increase indefinitely, which is precisely why a near point exists.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Analyze light dispersion, atmospheric refraction (twinkling), and Rayleigh scattering (blue sky/red sunset).

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Explain why the clear sky appears blue during the day.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Because the fine molecules of air scatter shorter blue wavelengths much more strongly than longer red wavelengths.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: According to Rayleigh scattering, the scattered intensity is much greater for shorter wavelengths. Air molecules therefore scatter blue light far more than red, and this scattered blue light reaching the eye from all directions makes the sky look blue.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Analyze light dispersion, atmospheric refraction (twinkling), and Rayleigh scattering (blue sky/red sunset).

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: White light splits into its constituent colours on passing through a glass prism because
options: the prism adds new colours to the light
all colours travel with the same speed in glass
the prism reflects each colour separately
different colours are refracted through different angles
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: different colours are refracted through different angles
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Each colour has a different speed in glass and hence a different refractive index, so each is deviated by a different amount, producing a spectrum.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Analyze light dispersion, atmospheric refraction (twinkling), and Rayleigh scattering (blue sky/red sunset).

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Explain why the sun appears reddish at sunrise and sunset.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Near the horizon sunlight travels a long path through the atmosphere, so most of the blue light is scattered away and mainly red light reaches the observer.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: At sunrise and sunset the light must pass through a much greater thickness of atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths are scattered out of the direct beam, leaving predominantly the longer red wavelengths to reach the eye.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Analyze light dispersion, atmospheric refraction (twinkling), and Rayleigh scattering (blue sky/red sunset).

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Explain why stars twinkle but planets generally do not.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Stars are point sources whose light is refracted by continually changing layers of air, whereas planets are extended sources whose many points average out.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Atmospheric refraction changes constantly as air layers move, so the apparent position and brightness of a point-like star fluctuate. A planet subtends a larger angle and acts as a collection of point sources whose variations cancel, so its light appears steady.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Analyze light dispersion, atmospheric refraction (twinkling), and Rayleigh scattering (blue sky/red sunset).

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Among the colours of the visible spectrum passing through a prism, the greatest deviation is suffered by
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: violet
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Violet has the shortest wavelength and the greatest refractive index in glass, so it is deviated most.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Analyze light dispersion, atmospheric refraction (twinkling), and Rayleigh scattering (blue sky/red sunset).

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
After a shower, an observer standing with the sun behind sees a rainbow in the sky.

Name the three optical effects that together produce the rainbow in the water droplets.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Refraction, internal reflection and dispersion of sunlight in the droplets.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Sunlight refracts on entering a droplet and disperses into colours, reflects internally at the rear surface, and refracts again on leaving, so the separated colours emerge in different directions and form the arc.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

outcome.title: Analyze light dispersion, atmospheric refraction (twinkling), and Rayleigh scattering (blue sky/red sunset).

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
Assertion (A): The sun is visible a little before actual sunrise.
Reason (R): Light from the sun bends as it passes through atmospheric layers of increasing density.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Atmospheric refraction bends the sunlight towards the observer, so the sun's apparent position is higher than its true position and it becomes visible about two minutes early.

outcome.title: Construct ray diagrams for concave/convex mirrors and apply the mirror formula.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Using the mirror formula and the standard sign convention, find the position of the image.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 15 cm in front of the mirror, that is v = -15 cm
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: With u = -30 cm and f = -10 cm, 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = -1/10 + 1/30 = -1/15, so v = -15 cm and the image forms 15 cm in front of the mirror.

outcome.title: Construct ray diagrams for concave/convex mirrors and apply the mirror formula.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: The image formed by a convex mirror of an object placed in front of it is always
options: virtual, inverted and of the same size
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: virtual, erect and diminished
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: A convex mirror diverges the reflected rays, so the image is always formed behind the mirror, erect and smaller than the object.

outcome.title: Construct ray diagrams for concave/convex mirrors and apply the mirror formula.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: An object is placed 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Find the magnification of the image and state its nature.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Magnification -1; the image is real, inverted and of the same size
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: With u = -20 cm and f = -10 cm, 1/v = -1/10 + 1/20 = -1/20, so v = -20 cm and m = -v/u = -(-20)/(-20) = -1. The negative value indicates a real inverted image of the same size, formed at the centre of curvature.

outcome.title: Construct ray diagrams for concave/convex mirrors and apply the mirror formula.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: An object is placed 15 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 10 cm. Find the position of the image.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 6 cm behind the mirror, that is v = +6 cm
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: With u = -15 cm and f = +10 cm, 1/v = 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6, so v = +6 cm and the virtual image lies 6 cm behind the mirror.

outcome.title: Construct ray diagrams for concave/convex mirrors and apply the mirror formula.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: The focal length of a spherical mirror of radius of curvature 24 cm is
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 12 cm
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: For a spherical mirror the focal length is half the radius of curvature, so f = 24/2 = 12 cm.

outcome.title: Construct ray diagrams for concave/convex mirrors and apply the mirror formula.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
Vehicle manufacturers fit a convex mirror rather than a plane mirror as the rear-view mirror on the driver's side.

Give two reasons, in terms of image formation, for this choice.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: It always gives an erect virtual image, and it has a much wider field of view.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: A convex mirror diverges reflected rays, so it always produces an erect, diminished virtual image and covers a far wider field of view than a plane mirror of the same size, letting the driver see more of the traffic behind.

outcome.title: Construct ray diagrams for concave/convex mirrors and apply the mirror formula.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
Assertion (A): A concave mirror can form a magnified erect image.
Reason (R): When the object lies between the pole and the principal focus of a concave mirror, the reflected rays diverge.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: For an object inside the focus, the reflected rays diverge and appear to come from behind the mirror, giving an erect and magnified virtual image, which is why shaving and dentist's mirrors are concave.

outcome.title: Apply Snell's law, solve thin-lens equations, and calculate optical power in dioptres.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Using the lens formula, find the position of the image.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 60 cm on the other side of the lens, that is v = +60 cm
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: With u = -30 cm and f = +20 cm, 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60, so v = +60 cm and a real image forms 60 cm beyond the lens.

outcome.title: Apply Snell's law, solve thin-lens equations, and calculate optical power in dioptres.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Find the power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm, stating the unit.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: +4 dioptre
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Power is the reciprocal of the focal length in metres, so P = 1/0.25 = +4 D, the positive sign indicating a converging lens.

outcome.title: Apply Snell's law, solve thin-lens equations, and calculate optical power in dioptres.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: An object is placed 20 cm from a concave lens of focal length 20 cm. Find the position of the image.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 10 cm from the lens on the same side as the object, that is v = -10 cm
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: With u = -20 cm and f = -20 cm, 1/v = -1/20 - 1/20 = -1/10, so v = -10 cm and the virtual image lies 10 cm from the lens on the object side.

outcome.title: Apply Snell's law, solve thin-lens equations, and calculate optical power in dioptres.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: A concave lens has a focal length of 50 cm. Find its power.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: -2 dioptre
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: P = 1/f in metres = 1/(-0.5) = -2 D, and the negative sign shows the lens is diverging.

outcome.title: Apply Snell's law, solve thin-lens equations, and calculate optical power in dioptres.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: A ray of light passes from air into water. The ray
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: bends towards the normal
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Water is optically denser than air, so on entering it the ray slows and bends towards the normal, in agreement with Snell's law.

outcome.title: Apply Snell's law, solve thin-lens equations, and calculate optical power in dioptres.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
A coin lying at the bottom of a bucket of clear water appears to be raised when viewed from directly above.

Name the phenomenon responsible and explain the observation.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Refraction of light; rays from the coin bend away from the normal on leaving water, so the coin appears nearer the surface.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Light leaving the denser water for the rarer air bends away from the normal. The eye traces these rays back in straight lines, so the image of the coin is formed above the coin's real position and the bottom appears raised.

outcome.title: Apply Snell's law, solve thin-lens equations, and calculate optical power in dioptres.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
Assertion (A): A lens of short focal length has a large power.
Reason (R): The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length expressed in metres.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Because power varies inversely with focal length, a shorter focal length gives a larger numerical power.

outcome.title: State Ohm's Law, calculate equivalent resistances, and analyze factors affecting electrical resistivity.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: A potential difference of 12 V is applied across a resistor of 4 ohm. Find the current in the resistor.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 3 A
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: By Ohm's law I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A.

outcome.title: State Ohm's Law, calculate equivalent resistances, and analyze factors affecting electrical resistivity.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Three resistors of 2 ohm, 3 ohm and 5 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 10 ohm
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: In series the equivalent resistance is the sum, 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 ohm.

outcome.title: State Ohm's Law, calculate equivalent resistances, and analyze factors affecting electrical resistivity.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Two resistors of 6 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 2 ohm
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: For a parallel combination 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so R = 2 ohm.

outcome.title: State Ohm's Law, calculate equivalent resistances, and analyze factors affecting electrical resistivity.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: A current of 0.5 A flows through a resistor of 24 ohm. Find the potential difference across it.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: By Ohm's law V = IR = 0.5 x 24 = 12 V.

outcome.title: State Ohm's Law, calculate equivalent resistances, and analyze factors affecting electrical resistivity.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: A wire of length 2 m and uniform cross-sectional area 0.5 square millimetre has resistivity 1.6 x 10^-8 ohm metre. Find its resistance.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: R = rho L / A with A = 0.5 x 10^-6 square metre, so R = (1.6 x 10^-8 x 2) / (5 x 10^-7) = 0.064 ohm.

outcome.title: State Ohm's Law, calculate equivalent resistances, and analyze factors affecting electrical resistivity.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: When several resistors are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance is
options: equal to the sum of the resistances
equal to the average of the resistances
less than the smallest individual resistance
greater than the largest individual resistance
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: less than the smallest individual resistance
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Adding a parallel path provides an extra route for current, so the combined resistance falls below that of any single branch.

outcome.title: State Ohm's Law, calculate equivalent resistances, and analyze factors affecting electrical resistivity.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
Assertion (A): A thicker wire of the same material and length has a lower resistance than a thinner one.
Reason (R): The resistance of a conductor is inversely proportional to its area of cross-section.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Since R = rho L / A, increasing the cross-sectional area decreases the resistance for a fixed material and length.

outcome.title: Apply Joule's Law of Heating and compute commercial electrical energy consumption in kWh.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: A current of 2 A flows through a resistor of 5 ohm for 10 s. Using Joule's law, find the heat produced.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: H = I^2 R t = 4 x 5 x 10 = 200 joule.

outcome.title: Apply Joule's Law of Heating and compute commercial electrical energy consumption in kWh.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: One kilowatt hour is equal to
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 3.6 x 10^6 joule
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: One kilowatt hour is 1000 watt x 3600 second = 3.6 x 10^6 joule.

outcome.title: Apply Joule's Law of Heating and compute commercial electrical energy consumption in kWh.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Four bulbs of 100 W each are used for 5 hours a day. Find the electrical energy consumed in 30 days, in kilowatt hours.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 60 kWh
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Energy = 4 x 100 x 5 x 30 watt hour = 60000 Wh = 60 kWh.

outcome.title: Apply Joule's Law of Heating and compute commercial electrical energy consumption in kWh.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: An electric heater of 1500 W runs for 2 hours a day for 20 days. If the tariff is 6 rupees per unit, find the total cost.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: 360 rupees
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Energy = 1.5 x 2 x 20 = 60 kWh, so the cost is 60 x 6 = 360 rupees.

outcome.title: Apply Joule's Law of Heating and compute commercial electrical energy consumption in kWh.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: An appliance draws a current of 5 A from a 220 V supply. Find its power.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Electric power is the product of the potential difference and the current, so P = VI = 220 x 5 = 1100 watt, that is 1.1 kilowatt.

outcome.title: Apply Joule's Law of Heating and compute commercial electrical energy consumption in kWh.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
The heating element of an electric iron is made of an alloy while its connecting cable is made of copper.

Explain this choice of materials in terms of the heating effect of current.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: The alloy has a high resistivity and a high melting point so it produces the heat, while copper has a very low resistivity so the cable stays cool.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Heat produced varies as I^2 R t. A high resistance element dissipates a large amount of heat and its high melting point prevents it from melting, whereas the low resistance copper cable dissipates very little heat and conducts the current safely.

outcome.title: Apply Joule's Law of Heating and compute commercial electrical energy consumption in kWh.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
Assertion (A): Doubling the current through a fixed resistor for the same time makes the heat produced four times as great.
Reason (R): The heat produced in a resistor is proportional to the square of the current.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Since H = I^2 R t, replacing I by 2I multiplies the heat by 2^2 = 4 when R and t are unchanged.

outcome.title: Determine magnetic field patterns using Right-Hand Thumb Rule for straight conductors, circular loops, and solenoids.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: State the right-hand thumb rule and use it to describe the field around a long straight wire carrying current vertically upwards, as seen from above.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: The field lines are concentric circles around the wire, directed anticlockwise when seen from above.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: If the wire is grasped in the right hand with the thumb pointing along the current, the curled fingers give the direction of the field. With the current upwards, the field circles the wire anticlockwise when viewed from above.

outcome.title: Determine magnetic field patterns using Right-Hand Thumb Rule for straight conductors, circular loops, and solenoids.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Two magnetic field lines can never intersect each other because
options: field lines are only imaginary and have no direction
at the point of intersection the field would have two directions, which is impossible
field lines always begin at the south pole
the field is strongest at points of intersection
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: at the point of intersection the field would have two directions, which is impossible
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The tangent to a field line gives the direction of the field at that point, and the field at a point can have only one direction.

outcome.title: Determine magnetic field patterns using Right-Hand Thumb Rule for straight conductors, circular loops, and solenoids.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Describe the magnetic field inside a current-carrying solenoid and state one use of this arrangement.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: The field inside is uniform and parallel to the axis, resembling that of a bar magnet; it is used to magnetise a soft iron core to form an electromagnet.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Inside a long solenoid the field lines are straight, equally spaced and parallel, so the field is uniform. Placing a soft iron core inside makes a strong electromagnet used in devices such as electric bells.

outcome.title: Determine magnetic field patterns using Right-Hand Thumb Rule for straight conductors, circular loops, and solenoids.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: How does the strength of the magnetic field at the centre of a circular current-carrying loop change if the number of turns is increased from 1 to 5, the current remaining unchanged?
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: It becomes five times as strong.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The fields due to the individual turns are in the same direction at the centre and add, so with n turns the field is n times that of a single turn.

outcome.title: Determine magnetic field patterns using Right-Hand Thumb Rule for straight conductors, circular loops, and solenoids.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Outside a bar magnet, the magnetic field lines are directed
options: from the middle of the magnet outwards
from the north pole to the south pole
from the south pole to the north pole
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: from the north pole to the south pole
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: By convention field lines emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole outside the magnet, completing the loop inside it.

outcome.title: Determine magnetic field patterns using Right-Hand Thumb Rule for straight conductors, circular loops, and solenoids.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
A small compass is placed near a straight horizontal wire. When the switch is closed and current flows, the compass needle is deflected.

What does this observation establish, and what happens if the direction of the current is reversed?
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: It establishes that a current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field; reversing the current reverses the deflection.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The deflection shows a magnetic field exists around the conductor. Because the direction of the field follows the right-hand thumb rule, reversing the current reverses the field and hence the direction of the needle's deflection.

outcome.title: Determine magnetic field patterns using Right-Hand Thumb Rule for straight conductors, circular loops, and solenoids.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
Assertion (A): The magnetic field is stronger where the field lines are crowded together.
Reason (R): The number of field lines per unit area represents the strength of the field.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Closely spaced lines mean more lines cross unit area, which by convention represents a stronger field.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: State Fleming's left-hand rule and name the quantity indicated by each of the three fingers.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: With the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand held mutually perpendicular, the forefinger shows the field, the middle finger the current and the thumb the force.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The rule gives the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field: forefinger for field, central finger for current and thumb for the resulting motion or force.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: The earth wire in a domestic circuit is provided mainly to
options: convert alternating current to direct current
give a low resistance path to earth so that the metal body of an appliance stays at earth potential
increase the current supplied to the appliance
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: give a low resistance path to earth so that the metal body of an appliance stays at earth potential
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: If a live wire touches the metal casing, the earth wire carries the current safely to the ground, preventing a severe shock to the user.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.topic: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor and Domestic Circuits

outcome.title: Apply Fleming's Left-Hand Rule to force vectors and detail safety features in domestic electric circuits.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Explain the function of a fuse in a domestic circuit and state the property of the fuse wire that makes it suitable.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: It melts and breaks the circuit when the current exceeds a safe value; the fuse wire has a low melting point and suitable resistance.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: During a short circuit or overload the current rises sharply and the heat produced, being proportional to I^2 R t, melts the thin fuse wire, breaking the circuit and protecting the appliances and wiring.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.topic: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor and Domestic Circuits

outcome.title: Apply Fleming's Left-Hand Rule to force vectors and detail safety features in domestic electric circuits.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: A straight conductor carrying current from north to south is placed in a magnetic field directed vertically downwards. Use Fleming's left-hand rule to find the direction of the force on the conductor.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: The force acts towards the east.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: With the forefinger pointing downwards for the field and the middle finger pointing from north to south for the current, the thumb of the left hand points towards the east, giving the direction of the force.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.topic: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor and Domestic Circuits

outcome.title: Apply Fleming's Left-Hand Rule to force vectors and detail safety features in domestic electric circuits.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Overloading of a domestic circuit occurs mainly when
options: the earth wire is properly connected
a fuse of correct rating is used
the live and neutral wires are correctly insulated
too many appliances of high power are used on the same circuit at once
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: too many appliances of high power are used on the same circuit at once
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Each appliance draws current in parallel, so running several high power appliances together raises the total current beyond the safe rating of the wiring.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.topic: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor and Domestic Circuits

outcome.title: Apply Fleming's Left-Hand Rule to force vectors and detail safety features in domestic electric circuits.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
In a household wiring system the live wire, the neutral wire and the earth wire are given different coloured insulation, and appliances are connected in parallel.

Give two reasons for connecting domestic appliances in parallel.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Each appliance gets the full supply voltage, and each can be switched on or off independently without affecting the others.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: A parallel arrangement keeps the potential difference across every appliance equal to the supply voltage and allows separate switches, so a fault in one branch does not stop the rest of the circuit.

outcome.title: Apply Fleming's Left-Hand Rule to force vectors and detail safety features in domestic electric circuits.

Assertion (A): A fuse is always connected in the live wire of a circuit.
Reason (R): Placing the fuse in the live wire disconnects the supply from the appliance when the fuse blows.
Choose the correct option.

A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: In a food chain the producers capture 10000 J of energy. Using the ten per cent law, find the energy available to the third trophic level.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Only about ten per cent passes to each successive level, so 10000 J gives 1000 J at the second level and 100 J at the third.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Name the two broad components of an ecosystem and give one example of each.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Biotic components such as plants and animals, and abiotic components such as air, water, soil and temperature.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: An ecosystem consists of all the living organisms in an area together with the non-living physical factors with which they interact.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Organisms that break down dead remains and return nutrients to the soil are called
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: decomposers
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Bacteria and fungi decompose dead organic matter and recycle nutrients into the environment.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
A pesticide sprayed on a crop field is washed into a nearby pond. Traces are later found in the water, then in small fish, and finally in fish-eating birds, where the concentration is highest.

Name this phenomenon and explain why the concentration rises along the chain.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Biological magnification; the chemical is not degraded or excreted, so it accumulates at each higher trophic level.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Because the pesticide is non-biodegradable, each consumer takes in the whole quantity present in the many organisms it eats but excretes very little, so the concentration in body tissues increases at every successive trophic level.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Explain why food chains in nature usually consist of only three or four trophic levels.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Because only about ten per cent of the energy is transferred at each step, too little energy remains to support further levels.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The loss of energy as heat and in life processes at every transfer means the energy available shrinks rapidly, so beyond three or four levels there is not enough to sustain a population.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
Assertion (A): The flow of energy in an ecosystem is unidirectional.
Reason (R): Energy enters as sunlight, passes through the trophic levels and is finally lost as heat.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Energy is not returned to the sun, so it flows in one direction only, unlike nutrients which are recycled.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: State whether the following is true or false, and justify in one line: Green plants occupy the first trophic level in a food chain.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: True
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Green plants are producers that capture solar energy, so they form the first trophic level.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: The producers of a food chain trap 20000 J of solar energy. Using the ten per cent law, find the energy available to the fourth trophic level.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Each transfer retains one tenth, so the levels hold 20000 J, 2000 J, 200 J and 20 J respectively.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Distinguish between a food chain and a food web in one sentence each, giving one advantage of a food web.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: A food chain is a single linear sequence of who eats whom, while a food web is the network of interconnected chains; the web gives an organism alternative food sources and so greater stability.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: In nature most organisms feed on more than one type of food, so the many chains interlink to form a web, which makes the ecosystem less vulnerable to the loss of a single species.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: In the food chain grass to grasshopper to frog to snake, the frog occupies the
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: third trophic level
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Grass is the first level, the grasshopper the second and the frog the third.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question:
A pond receives a discharge containing a non-biodegradable heavy metal. Concentrations are measured as 0.02 parts per million in the water, 0.5 in small fish and 8 in the birds that eat those fish.

Which trophic level is at greatest risk, and what property of the pollutant explains the pattern?
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: The birds, because the pollutant is non-biodegradable and undergoes biological magnification.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: The pollutant cannot be broken down or excreted, so it accumulates in tissues and its concentration increases sharply at each higher level, leaving the top consumers most affected.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: If 5000 J of energy is available at the second trophic level, how much reaches the fourth trophic level under the ten per cent law?
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: From the second to the third level 500 J is transferred, and from the third to the fourth 50 J.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: What would happen to an ecosystem if all its decomposers were removed?
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Dead remains and wastes would pile up and nutrients would not be returned to the soil, so producers would eventually fail.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Decomposers recycle nutrients locked in dead organic matter. Without them the nutrient cycle breaks, the soil is not replenished and plant growth, and hence the whole ecosystem, collapses.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Because decomposition releases nutrients back into soil, water and air, the same atoms are used again by producers, while energy is lost as heat.

outcome.title: Apply Lindeman's 10% Energy Law to food chains and evaluate biological magnification.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: An omnivore such as a human being can act as a primary consumer when eating plants and as a secondary consumer when eating animals.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Explain briefly how ozone is formed in the upper atmosphere and state why the ozone layer is important.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: High energy ultraviolet radiation splits oxygen molecules into free atoms which combine with oxygen molecules to form ozone; the layer shields living organisms from harmful ultraviolet radiation.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Ultraviolet radiation dissociates O2 into atomic oxygen, and these atoms combine with further O2 molecules to give O3. The resulting layer absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation that would otherwise cause skin cancer and damage crops.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Name the class of synthetic chemicals chiefly responsible for depleting the ozone layer and state one common use that has now been restricted.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.answer: Chlorofluorocarbons; they were widely used as refrigerants and as propellants in aerosol sprays.
SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons are very stable and drift to the stratosphere, where ultraviolet radiation releases chlorine atoms that destroy ozone molecules. Their production has therefore been frozen and phased down internationally.

A residential colony collects all its household waste in a single bin and sends it to a landfill. Residents notice a persistent stench and choked drains.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Separating the waste at source allows kitchen waste to be turned into compost and plastics, metals and glass to be sent for recycling, so far less material rots in the landfill and drains stay clear.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.explanation: Because microorganisms cannot break these materials down, they remain in the soil and water for decades, block drainage, injure or kill animals that swallow them, and pass along food chains where their concentration increases.

SCIENCE_EXPERT_REVIEW.question: Suggest two steps a municipality can take to reduce the quantity of non-biodegradable waste reaching its landfill.
